mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: RESPA Section 8 prohibits accepting or charging an unearned fee when no actual settlement service is performed. Merely disclosing the charge does not make it lawful.

distractorExplanations.a: Disclosure does not cure an unearned fee; RESPA Section 8(b) requires an actual settlement service to support the charge.
distractorExplanations.b: A finance-charge error may implicate TILA, but a fee collected without a performed service is specifically a RESPA Section 8 issue.
distractorExplanations.d: TRID tolerance cures address certain fee increases, not whether an underlying fee was earned through a real settlement service.

options.a: Permitted when the referring party gives the consumer an affiliated-business disclosure
options.b: Permitted when the payment is recorded on the Closing Disclosure
options.d: Permitted when the referral payment reflects the loan amount

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: RESPA Section 8 generally prohibits giving or accepting a fee, kickback, or thing of value under an agreement to refer federally related mortgage settlement business.

distractorExplanations.a: An affiliated-business disclosure does not authorize payment for referrals; the safe harbor requires separate conditions, including no required use.
distractorExplanations.b: Showing a kickback on the Closing Disclosure does not legalize it because disclosure cannot cure a prohibited referral-payment agreement.
distractorExplanations.d: Tying compensation to the loan amount does not make a referral fee lawful; RESPA focuses on the exchange of value for the referral.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Regulation Z's loan-originator compensation rule generally bars an originator from receiving compensation from both the consumer and another person, such as the creditor, on the same transaction.

distractorExplanations.b: Disclosure on the Closing Disclosure does not override Regulation Z's restriction on consumer-paid and creditor-paid compensation in one transaction.
distractorExplanations.c: Written consumer consent cannot waive the dual-compensation restriction imposed by the loan-originator compensation rule.
distractorExplanations.d: Dual compensation is principally a Regulation Z loan-originator compensation issue, not a RESPA violation that becomes lawful after a refund.

options.a: Requesting that a qualified appraiser analyze an additional comparable sale
options.b: Providing the appraiser with a signed purchase contract
options.c: Conditioning future assignments on reaching a target value
options.d: Asking the appraiser to correct a factual error in the report

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Appraiser-independence rules prohibit coercing, bribing, or intimidating an appraiser to reach a predetermined value. Legitimate requests for corrections or reconsideration remain allowed.

distractorExplanations.a: A good-faith request to consider relevant additional property information is allowed when it does not pressure the appraiser toward a target value.
distractorExplanations.b: Providing transaction documents needed for the assignment is ordinary factual communication and does not itself compromise appraiser independence.
distractorExplanations.d: A request to correct an objective factual error is permitted so long as it does not condition compensation or future work on a desired value.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: An MLO must stop and correct a known material misstatement before the information is submitted or relied upon. Knowingly forwarding false application data can facilitate mortgage fraud.

distractorExplanations.b: Passing known false information to underwriting is not cured by later review; the MLO must address the misstatement before submission.
distractorExplanations.c: A borrower cannot validate false information merely by initialing it at closing; the application and supporting record must be corrected promptly.
distractorExplanations.d: Waiting for an automated underwriting system to detect known false data is willful inaction and does not satisfy the MLO's ethical duty.

options.a: The SAFE Act's licensing and education provisions
options.c: The Fair Credit Reporting Act's dispute provisions
options.d: Fair Housing Act and fair-lending requirements

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: The Fair Housing Act protects applicants from housing-related discrimination based on familial status. An MLO may not treat families with children or pregnant applicants less favorably.

distractorExplanations.a: The SAFE Act governs MLO licensing, registration, testing, and education; it does not establish familial status as a protected class.
distractorExplanations.b: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act governs financial privacy and safeguarding customer information, not discrimination based on familial status.
distractorExplanations.c: The Fair Credit Reporting Act regulates consumer reports and dispute rights, rather than protected-class treatment in housing transactions.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Advertising a teaser rate that is not actually available as represented can be deceptive under federal advertising and UDAAP standards. Required disclosures do not cure a fundamentally misleading offer.

distractorExplanations.a: Stating an APR in fine print does not cure a headline rate that consumers cannot actually obtain under the represented terms.
distractorExplanations.b: An isolated past transaction does not support advertising a rate that is not reasonably available to the audience targeted by the current offer.
distractorExplanations.d: RESPA Section 8 addresses referral payments and unearned fees; misleading rate advertising instead raises TILA advertising and UDAAP concerns.

options.a: Acceptable if the borrower expects to visit the property regularly
options.b: Acceptable if owner-occupied pricing makes the payment affordable
options.c: Mortgage fraud and an MLO ethics violation
options.d: A disclosure error that can be cured before consummation

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Intended occupancy is material to mortgage eligibility, pricing, and risk. Encouraging a borrower to claim owner occupancy falsely is mortgage fraud and a serious ethical violation.

distractorExplanations.a: Occasional visits do not make a property the borrower's principal residence; occupancy must be represented according to the borrower's true intent.
distractorExplanations.b: A better rate or more affordable payment never justifies misstating occupancy because the representation affects underwriting and investor risk.
distractorExplanations.d: False occupancy is not merely a disclosure-timing defect; the application must accurately state the intended use of the property.

options.c: Determining whether collateral lies in a flood hazard area

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Fair-lending compliance requires consistent assistance, information, and access for similarly situated applicants without regard to prohibited bases under ECOA and other applicable laws.

distractorExplanations.a: Loan-level price adjustments reflect documented loan-risk attributes and do not define the duty to provide equal assistance across protected classes.
distractorExplanations.b: Debt-to-income calculation is an underwriting measurement; applying it consistently may support fair lending, but it is not the governing principle.
distractorExplanations.c: Flood-zone status is established through property-specific determinations, not through rules governing equal treatment of applicants.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: TRID implements integrated TILA-RESPA disclosures through the Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure, combining key loan-cost and settlement information in standardized forms.

distractorExplanations.a: The Good Faith Estimate and HUD-1 were legacy forms largely replaced by the Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure for TRID-covered loans.
distractorExplanations.b: Adverse-action notices and appraisal-copy delivery arise primarily under ECOA and Regulation B, outside the integrated LE and CD framework.
distractorExplanations.d: Initial escrow statements and servicing-transfer notices remain distinct Regulation X requirements rather than components of the TRID forms.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: For a TRID-covered mortgage, the creditor generally must deliver or place the Loan Estimate in the mail no later than the third business day after receiving an application.

distractorExplanations.b: Seven business days is generally the minimum period between delivery or mailing of the Loan Estimate and consummation, not the issuance deadline.
distractorExplanations.c: Ten business days relates to how long the estimated charges must remain available for acceptance, rather than when the Loan Estimate is due.
distractorExplanations.d: Thirty days is associated with Regulation B action-taken timing on a completed application, not the TRID Loan Estimate deadline.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: For a TRID-covered loan, the consumer generally must receive the Closing Disclosure at least three business days before consummation, subject to a narrow bona fide emergency waiver.

distractorExplanations.a: The former one-day HUD-1 inspection rule is not the current TRID receipt period for the Closing Disclosure.
distractorExplanations.c: Seven business days is associated with the Loan Estimate waiting period before consummation, not receipt of the Closing Disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: First providing the Closing Disclosure at consummation denies the consumer the required three-business-day review period.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Covered higher-priced mortgage loans generally require a written appraisal by a certified or licensed appraiser who performs a physical interior inspection, plus compliance with appraisal-independence protections.

distractorExplanations.a: An MLO may not pressure an appraiser toward a target value; appraisal independence applies regardless of who coordinates the order.
distractorExplanations.b: For a covered HPML, an automated valuation model alone does not replace the required written appraisal and physical interior inspection.
distractorExplanations.d: A second appraisal is limited to certain rapid-resale situations and may not be charged to the consumer; it is not required for every refinance.

options.a: Rejecting every transaction that includes a cash deposit
options.b: Telling a customer when a suspicious activity report is filed
options.c: Filing a suspicious activity report for every declined application
options.d: Maintaining an AML program and filing SARs when required

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Covered mortgage lenders and originators must maintain a risk-based anti-money-laundering program and file confidential suspicious activity reports when regulatory criteria are met.

distractorExplanations.a: Cash deposits require sourcing and risk review when relevant, but the BSA does not impose a blanket rejection rule for every cash component.
distractorExplanations.b: Suspicious activity reports are confidential; disclosing to a customer that a SAR was filed is prohibited tipping off.
distractorExplanations.c: A credit denial alone does not automatically require a SAR; filing depends on suspicious facts and applicable reporting thresholds.

options.a: The loan has a fixed interest rate for its full term
options.b: The APR, points and fees, or prepayment penalty meets an applicable high-cost threshold
options.c: The loan's annual percentage rate exceeds its note rate
options.d: The creditor intends to sell the loan in the secondary market

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: HOEPA coverage is determined by statutory high-cost triggers involving APR, points and fees, or certain prepayment-penalty terms. Covered loans receive added disclosures and restrictions.

distractorExplanations.a: A fixed rate does not itself make a mortgage high-cost; the transaction must meet one of HOEPA's quantitative coverage triggers.
distractorExplanations.c: APR commonly exceeds the note rate because it reflects certain finance charges, but that fact alone does not establish HOEPA coverage.
distractorExplanations.d: An intended secondary-market sale does not determine high-cost status; HOEPA applies according to the loan's terms and coverage thresholds.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: The front-end debt-to-income ratio divides the proposed monthly housing expense, commonly principal, interest, taxes, and insurance, by the borrower's gross monthly income.

distractorExplanations.a: Including housing and all recurring monthly obligations produces the back-end DTI ratio, not the front-end housing ratio.
distractorExplanations.b: Non-housing installment obligations are considered in back-end DTI; front-end DTI focuses on the proposed housing expense.
distractorExplanations.c: Dividing a housing payment by property value is not front-end DTI because the denominator must be gross monthly income.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.prompt: A lender originates a conventional loan that meets conforming loan limits and underwriting standards. Which secondary-market outlet commonly purchases this type of loan?

options.a: Ginnie Mae, which purchases conventional loans directly from lenders
options.b: The FDIC, which buys mortgages to protect depositor accounts
options.c: Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac under applicable delivery requirements
options.d: The FHA, which purchases conforming loans after endorsement

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac commonly purchase eligible conforming conventional loans from approved sellers, helping provide liquidity in the secondary mortgage market.

distractorExplanations.a: Ginnie Mae guarantees securities backed by government-insured or guaranteed loans; it does not directly buy conforming conventional loans.
distractorExplanations.b: The FDIC insures qualifying bank deposits and resolves failed institutions; it is not a routine purchaser of conforming mortgages.
distractorExplanations.d: FHA insures eligible mortgages made by approved lenders; it does not purchase conventional loans in the secondary market.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: A primary residence is the dwelling the borrower genuinely intends to occupy as the principal home. Occupancy intent affects underwriting, pricing, and required representations.

distractorExplanations.a: Part-year or occasional occupancy may describe a second home; a primary residence must serve as the borrower's principal dwelling.
distractorExplanations.b: A property acquired primarily for rent while the borrower lives elsewhere is generally an investment property, not a primary residence.
distractorExplanations.d: Using an address for mail does not establish principal occupancy; the borrower must genuinely intend to live there as the main home.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: A jumbo mortgage exceeds the applicable conforming loan limit and therefore is not eligible for standard Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac purchase as a conforming loan.

distractorExplanations.a: FHA county limits determine eligibility for FHA insurance, while jumbo status is measured against applicable conforming loan limits.
distractorExplanations.c: Loan-to-value measures leverage rather than loan size; a high-LTV loan may still fall within the conforming loan limit.
distractorExplanations.d: Two- to four-unit properties have separate conforming limits, so the property's unit count alone does not make the mortgage jumbo.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.prompt: After receiving a complete application, an MLO notices that the borrower's bank statement shows a large recent deposit. What is the appropriate next step?

options.a: Exclude the entire bank account from the application without asking the borrower
options.b: Ask for documentation that explains and verifies the source of the deposit
options.c: Treat the deposit as verified income because it appears on a bank statement
options.d: Move the deposit to the gift-funds section so underwriting will accept it

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: A large recent deposit may affect the validity of funds used for closing. The MLO should obtain a credible explanation and documentation so underwriting can evaluate an acceptable source.

distractorExplanations.a: Automatically excluding the account may discard valid assets; the proper response is to investigate and document the deposit's source.
distractorExplanations.c: Appearance on a bank statement proves the deposit occurred, not that it is income or an acceptable source of closing funds.
distractorExplanations.d: Funds may be classified as a gift only when they actually meet program rules and are supported by the required donor documentation.

options.a: The borrower makes a down payment of at least 20 percent
options.b: The conventional loan has a loan-to-value ratio above 80 percent
options.c: The lender escrows property taxes and homeowners insurance
options.d: The conventional loan has a fixed rather than adjustable rate

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: On many conventional first mortgages, private mortgage insurance is required when the initial loan-to-value ratio exceeds 80 percent, subject to program-specific rules.

distractorExplanations.a: A down payment of at least 20 percent generally produces an LTV of 80 percent or less, where borrower-paid PMI is usually unnecessary.
distractorExplanations.c: Escrowing taxes and homeowners insurance concerns payment administration and does not by itself trigger private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.d: Both fixed-rate and adjustable-rate conventional loans may require PMI; the principal trigger is leverage, not rate structure.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: After any initial fixed period, an ARM's fully indexed rate is generally calculated using the specified index plus a fixed margin, subject to initial, periodic, and lifetime caps.

distractorExplanations.a: The margin ordinarily remains fixed under the note while the index changes; adjustment caps may then limit the resulting rate movement.
distractorExplanations.c: ARM adjustments follow the contract's specified index and margin, not an interest rate changed solely at the lender's discretion.
distractorExplanations.d: Credit characteristics affect initial eligibility and pricing, but scheduled ARM adjustments do not recalculate from the borrower's current credit score.

options.a: Obtain a lower note rate by paying additional upfront cost
options.b: Reduce the required down payment without changing the loan amount
options.c: Prepay the first year of property taxes through the lender
options.d: Increase the appraised value used in the loan-to-value calculation

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Discount points are an upfront finance charge paid in exchange for a lower interest rate. One point equals one percent of the loan amount, though the rate reduction varies.

distractorExplanations.b: Discount points change the interest-rate pricing, not the relationship between purchase price, loan amount, and required down payment.
distractorExplanations.c: Property-tax deposits fund an escrow account and are separate from discount points paid to reduce the mortgage interest rate.
distractorExplanations.d: An appraised value must come from an independent valuation; paying points cannot alter collateral value or the resulting LTV calculation.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: A balloon mortgage is amortized over a period longer than its stated term, leaving a substantial unpaid principal balance due in one lump sum at maturity.

distractorExplanations.a: Payments that respond to movement in an index describe an adjustable-rate mortgage, not the defining maturity feature of a balloon loan.
distractorExplanations.b: Predetermined payment increases describe a graduated-payment mortgage; a balloon loan is defined by the large balance due at maturity.
distractorExplanations.c: An interest-only period can later convert to amortizing payments without a balloon; the defining feature is an unpaid lump sum due at maturity.

mortgage-loan-originator-readiness-check.explanation: Loan-level price adjustments alter the cost or pricing of eligible conventional loans based on risk characteristics such as credit score, LTV, occupancy, and product features.

distractorExplanations.a: Mortgage-insurance coverage is governed by investor and insurer requirements; LLPAs instead adjust loan pricing for specified risk attributes.
distractorExplanations.c: Conforming limits and program rules determine maximum loan amounts, while LLPAs affect the price of an otherwise eligible loan.
distractorExplanations.d: Underwriting and automated systems determine eligibility or approval; LLPAs set pricing adjustments after considering defined risk characteristics.
